climateNote: This is a tectonic event: steady aseismic creep on a transform fault. No climate connection is claimed — it is included for the fault-slip radar physics lesson and the decade-long window.

dataset.mission: Sentinel-1A/1B (Copernicus), ascending pass; decade-long studies also use ERS/Envisat
dataset.datasetId: USGS creep-meter and GNSS series; Copernicus Sentinel-1 SLC
dataset.window: Published: multi-decade creep record (Titus et al., 2006); in-app pass-pair window: 3,600 days
dataset.coverage: Central California — San Juan Bautista to Parkfield creeping section (~90 km scene)
dataset.gnss: POMM + CARL, Nevada Geodetic Lab daily IGS20 solutions, bundled as weekly means
dataset.processing: Published: creep meters, aligned arrays, GNSS velocities. In-app: elastic rectangular dislocation (25 cm slip at 12 km depth); one fringe = λ/2 line-of-sight motion

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: Real daily IGS20 solutions from NGL stations POMM and CARL, downsampled to weekly means, bundled and charted in-app.

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: ~25 mm/yr surface creep near the center of the creeping section (Titus et al., 2006, BSSA). Shown as citation; not re-derived in-app.

items.label: MODELED
items.detail: Physics rendering of a rectangular dislocation source (25 cm slip). NOT a raw SAR image — computed on-device.

items.label: DERIVED
items.detail: Computed on-device from the physical model (one fringe = λ/2 LOS). Tracks the model, not a downloaded product.

items.label: LIVE
items.detail: Live accelerometer from the demo ESP32 ground station — IoT demo at the demo site; not a satellite measurement of this event.

limitations: The interferogram is a physics rendering of published figures, not raw SAR pixels — no SAR processing is done in-app.
Creep rate varies along strike and with depth; the uniform-slip model is a simplification.
Over the 3,600-day window the signal is under one L-band fringe; the band selector exists precisely for this case.
